reviews.quote: I Tested HP's OmniBook Ultra 14, a Gorgeous Ultraportable With Potent Processing Power

praises: 3K OLED touch panel at 120Hz is the standout — deep blacks and smooth scroll in a sub-1.4kg chassis
85 TOPS NPU runs Copilot+ local models (Phi-family) without melting the lap
Genuinely quiet under office load; fan barely audible per PCMag-style testing of the line
Quad Poly speakers noticeably better than most 14-inch thin-and-lights on video calls
All-day battery in mixed ARM Windows use — X2 Elite sips power at idle
complaints: ARM Windows app-translation gaps remain for niche drivers and anti-cheat games
$3,300 CAD at Best Buy with no discount while Lunar Lake sibling sells for far less
Soldered RAM and storage — no upgrade path at any price
Touch OLED draws extra battery vs non-touch tiers
HP bloat (Wolf security trials, Smart Sense) ships preloaded

design_philosophy: HP's consumer flagship clamshell: maximum screen quality and NPU punch in a slim aluminium shell, aimed at premium productivity users who want OLED and Copilot+ AI without gaming GPU weight. The X2 Elite tier is the efficiency/AI end of the line.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from PCMag's reviewed OmniBook Ultra 14 config (headline quote verified; numeric score not retrievable — fetch 403) adjusted for X2 Elite: +1 ai_ml (85 TOPS vs 45-48 TOPS), +0.5 battery, -0.5 gaming vs Adreno/X-Elite class. ARM ecosystem 7.5 per dataset convention. Image URL follows verified Best Buy CDN pattern from SKU.
